newsitem.title: GREECE: Dutch reporter shot in Albania, rushed to Greece.
newsitem.headline: Dutch reporter shot in Albania, rushed to Greece.

text.p: A Dutch journalist was shot on Tuesday by a sniper in the Albanian port town of Sarande and rushed to hospital on the nearby Greek island of Corfu, witnesses said.

Wilma Goudappel, a freelance reporter covering the violent uprising in the tiny Balkan country, was shot by a sniper at the door of the house she was renting, a colleague who escorted her to Corfu told Greek television.
"She had just opened the door and was speaking on the phone when a sniper shot her," the reporter said. He was not identified.
Doctors at the hospital told Greek reporters Goudappel was shot in the abdomen and was in serious condition but expected to recover.
She was rushed to Corfu on the small passenger ferry Kalliopi, the only regular link between Sarande and Greece.
Goudappel had been in Albania for weeks, covering an armed uprising against the government after the collapse of pyramid investment schemes that left thousands destitute.
